status: built_not_placed 2026-10-09: generated by tools/tri_peaks_nest.py into build/datapacks/cobblers_tri_peaks_nest on tools/resident_encounters.py's keeper; re-application step R9TP (blocks only). Not applied to any world; nothing here was observed in game
purpose: The Tri Peaks' open-summit nest (the sweep's gap 2, docs/world-building/WORLD_SWEEP_2026-10-09.md section 7): one big Pokemon IN THE OPEN on the bare crown of the massif's south peak, seen from Highwire before it can be reached. The Ursaluna den is the Tri Peaks' cave; this is its summit

rules.respawn_why: one hour of server time on the game clock, the Ursaluna den's cooldown (data/ursaluna_cave.json ursaluna.returns): long enough that the summit is a place you go back to, not one you farm. A 600-BST catch at gym 3 is the reason this is not the residents' 36,000
rules.keeper: tools/resident_encounters.py's persistent resident/guardian pattern, unchanged: never replace or despawn an entity tagged cobblers.guardian; blackout recovery belongs to that exact Pokemon
rules.aggression: Bounded local trigger and leash; never change Fight or Flight behaviour for the species globally.

design.why_this_creature: A big upright dark-and-stone Pokemon whose silhouette is its own skyline: black against a white or pale summit, 3.16 blocks tall (Cobblemon 1.8.0 species hitbox 2 x 3.16, read from the jar), the largest of the mountain candidates that is not already somewhere else. The Tri Peaks' summit heart is birds and Duraludon (data/encounter_design.json the_tri_peaks), so nothing up there is a rock giant; a Tyranitar fills the gap and is the one candidate whose natural story is that it takes mountains apart, which is what the place shows

why_not.aerodactyl_braviary: a perched bird on a high rock is the sea-stack rookery's shape (the C7 nest built tonight)
why_not.golem: data/northern_residents.json already has a Golem, a boulder on the glacier fields; a second boulder would read the same
why_not.avalugg_mamoswine: ice giants: Whiteback (Mamoswine) is a resident in A7, and the snow castle and the ice lodge are being built in A1 and the Merian cirque tonight
why_not.rhyperior: the sturdier fit for balance (BST 535 against 600) and the swap if the owner finds a 600-BST catch at gym 3 too much: two fields (species, and the message), nothing else changes. Not chosen because a rhino reads as a plains beast, and the evolution is by trade
why_not.steelix: a serpent along the crest was considered (the ridge that moves); its Attack of 85 makes meeting it early a delay, not a mistake

design.balance_flag: Tyranitar is a 600-BST pseudo-legendary caught at level 35 with the third badge. Stats are not set here (no moves, ability, nature or IV is written; the species learnset decides what it knows at 35). The owner decides whether that is the prize or too much; the swap is two fields
design.level: 35: strictly over the cap 30 a player carries before beating gym 3 (data/trainers.json generation_contract.gym_ace_levels[2]), at the cap 35 the third badge gives (gym_ace_levels[3]), and at the_tri_peaks' ceiling 35 (data/encounter_design.json rules.hearts.next_cap['3']). Its band is 20-28: seven above its top, five over the cap of a player who has not yet beaten Surge. The level-cap refusal (data/level_cap.json) is the catch gate
design.place: the bare crown of the south peak, an open dome (y250 to y253 across the 7-block bench, measured), ringed by six rock teeth with a breach to the south where the broken tooth's rubble pours down a 112-block scree spur to the shoulder at y190 above Highwire. Not a cave, not a building, not a path: a summit and the slope you climb to it
design.seen_from_below: the crown's teeth are 7-12 blocks tall on a dome (y253; the north-west summit (1372, 840) is y255, 246 blocks away, and the massif's highest columns, (1848, 1352) at y287 and Mt Vessu's (1864, 760) at y300, are 470 and 490 blocks east), which Highwire sees over the ground between (measured below), so they read as a serrated crown on the skyline north-north-west of the town. Measured on the heightmap: the tallest tooth's tip (1474, 263, 1053) is in line of sight from the town centre, 416 blocks away, clear of the ground between by 2.3 blocks (a margin, not a wide one: eye 1.7 above the ground), and from Route 3 for its last 115 path points, from (1721, 1524), 532 blocks out (tools/tri_peaks_nest.py --report). ASSUMED, not observed: that the blocks show that far. The server's view-distance is 10 chunks (server/config/server.properties.example) so the vanilla chunks do not; Distant Horizons is in the overlay (modpack/manifest/overlay.json) and draws LODs of saved chunks, which would carry the teeth once the dressed chunks are saved and the LODs refresh. The creature itself exists only while a player is within 96 blocks (the keeper's spawn_radius, the simulation distance 6 chunks) and renders only inside the client's entity distance (ASSUMED vanilla: 64 blocks times the mean of its bounding box edges), so the figure is seen on the scree and the crown from town
design.approach: a walk, no placed blocks: from Highwire's gate (1688, 1412) a path in which no step between adjacent columns is over one block exists (A* over the rounded heightmap, 8 neighbours; tests/test_tri_peaks_nest.py recomputes it): 437 blocks with 110 of climb to the crown; 314 of them (46 of climb) to the scree's toe at (1476, 1186), then 126 blocks (64 of climb) up inside the scree strip itself, where the creature faces down the slope toward the town

measured.by: 2026-10-09, tools/ground.py rounded heightmap, throwaway scripts; tests/test_tri_peaks_nest.py recomputes each with its own code
measured.units: blocks of horizontal walking distance and blocks of cumulative climb; path points are route_paths.json points, about 1.2 blocks apart

design.catchable_path: the climb crosses only the_tri_peaks' own tier-3 land and summit-heart tables; this nest adds no spawn
design.no_habitat_block: none added. The Ursaluna den's slope needs one for its cubs; here the existing summit heart (data/encounter_design.json the_tri_peaks heart, minY 195) already covers y195 and above, which is the crown and the spur down to about z1155 of its 1174 (ground y198 at z1150, y194 at z1158, measured)

old_jaw_blackout_check.judgement: not applicable: a resident that beats a player is an ordinary wild victor to the blackout (data/resident_encounters.json build.blackout_decision), becomes that claim's guardian, and this pack counts it and never touches it again
old_jaw_blackout_check.runtime_proof_needed: the same as the residents': a loss at the crown, then recovery by beating or catching that exact Pokemon

encounters.name: Crownbreaker

location.y_rule: feet one above the rounded canonical heightmap ground (tools/ground.py); x/z are this record's, measured: the dome's highest columns are y253 at x1474-1480, z1058-1064

encounters.build_brief: A bare dome ringed by six black rock teeth with a breach to the south; a scree spur from the breach down to the shoulder; heaps of rubble along it. Trigger 30, leash 40.

build.yaw_why: toward Highwire's gate: the bearing from the crown (1478, 1062) to the town centre (1688, 1410) is 31 degrees east of south, and Minecraft yaw 0 faces +z, negative turns toward +x
build.appears_after_why: none, on purpose: the brief is a creature a player sees before they are ready, so it stands there from the first time anyone is within 96 blocks of the crown. Its gate is the level cap (data/level_cap.json), as Old Jaw's is, not a presence flag
build.message: The black teeth around the summit are not all there is up there. One of the boulders straightens: Crownbreaker.
build.why: the south peak of the Tri Peaks, seen from Highwire as the skyline above the town's north-north-west. The bench is scoured bare so the creature stands on stone, not snow; the six teeth are the crown, tallest at the back (north-west, 12) and lowest at the front (south-west, 7); the south is open where the broken tooth fell and its rubble runs down the spur, widening to the toe. Everything is the stone family; the dark teeth are the silhouette
build.anchor_why: x/z are this record's, measured on the canonical heightmap (tools/ground.py); feet one above the rounded ground
build.bbox_why: every block the dressing writes and the anchor, inclusive [x0, z0, x1, z1]; R9TP force-loads exactly this box

keeper.why: tools/resident_encounters.py's keeper constants, unchanged (data/resident_encounters.json build.keeper.why). This pack has its own tag, dormant tag and objective so its clock and its holds never meet the ten residents'; the guardian tag is the blackout's and shared on purpose

build.trigger_rule: as data/resident_encounters.json build.trigger_rule: a state check on the keeper's loop, never an advancement; dormant (NoAI, on its spot, facing its yaw) until the first non-spectator player within `trigger` blocks of the anchor, then awake under its own AI and Fight or Flight's global config, which this pack never touches
build.appears_after_rule: none: this resident is ungated and the keeper brings it in the first time a player is within spawn_radius of the crown and none within spawn_clear. The only gate is the level cap
build.catch_rule_mechanism: the level-cap refusal (data/level_cap.json): a catch strictly above the thrower's RCT cap breaks free of any ball. L35 is over the cap 30 until the third badge and within the cap 35 after it
build.blackout_decision: as data/resident_encounters.json build.blackout_decision: this pack never adds cobblers.gm and, from the moment the resident carries cobblers.guardian, never touches it again
build.drops_rule: no loot drops: nothing in this pack gives, loots or summons an item
build.lighting: none added: an open summit, lit by the day
build.sound_and_message_why: placeholders in plain words; the voice is the owner's
